summary: This bill modifies work requirements for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) by extending the time limit for certain individuals and applying these work requirements to recipients of public housing and tenant-based rental assistance.

scores.thoughts: This bill modifies work requirements for SNAP and extends these requirements to public housing and tenant-based rental assistance. By potentially reducing the number of eligible recipients for these programs, it aims to decrease government outlays, thus leading to less government spending.

The bill tightens work requirements for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and extends these requirements to public housing and tenant-based rental assistance. This would likely reduce the number of beneficiaries and the scope of these programs, thereby reducing welfare spending and contracting the social safety net.

The bill tightens SNAP work requirements and extends them to public housing and rental assistance, which would reduce program participation and federal spending. While the legislation's primary focus is work requirements rather than fiscal policy, this change has a minor positive effect on deficit reduction.
